text_version.note: AGORA record covers part of an act: An Act concerning the use of automated tools to assist with hiring decisions and supplementing Title 34 of the Revised S

territorial_scope.description: Applies to sales and offers for sale of automated employment decision tools in the State of New Jersey.

evidence.quote: It shall be unlawful to sell or offer for sale in the State an automated employment decision tool unless:

summary.short: Pending New Jersey bill making it unlawful to sell or offer for sale in the State an automated employment decision tool without a bias audit in the past year, an annual audit service and a notice. Users must notify candidates within 30 days; the act takes effect immediately.
summary.long: Pending New Jersey bill that supplements Title 34 and defines an automated employment decision tool as a system that automatically filters candidates for hire or for any term, condition or privilege of employment in a way that establishes a preferred candidate. It makes it unlawful to sell or offer for sale in the State such a tool unless it has been the subject of a bias audit conducted in the past year, the sale includes at no additional cost an annual bias audit service that provides the results to the purchaser, and the tool is sold with a notice that it is subject to the act. Any person who uses such a tool to screen a candidate for an employment decision must notify each candidate within 30 days that the tool was used and that it assessed the candidate's job qualifications or characteristics. Violations carry a civil penalty of not more than $500 for a first violation and each additional violation on the same day, and not less than $500 nor more than $1,500 for each subsequent violation, accruing daily for each tool; each 30-day notice failure is a separate violation. Penalties are payable to the State Treasurer and may be recovered in a summary proceeding brought by the commissioner. The Department of Labor and Workforce Development, in consultation with the Division on Civil Rights, must promulgate rules. The act affirms candidates' rights without limiting other rights or enforcement authority, and takes effect immediately.

relations.target_text: Law Against Discrimination, P.L. 1945, c. 169 (C. 10:5-1 et seq.)
relations.note: The bias audit definition measures a tool's predicted compliance with the Law Against Discrimination and other employment discrimination law. Subsection g. states that the act does not reduce rights under other law.

notes: Bill text as introduced and pending; the self-citations 'P.L. , c. (C. )' are unfilled placeholders. Subsection d(2) makes a notice failure 'in violation of subsection b.', but the 30-day candidate notice duty is in subsection c; the cross-reference appears to be wrong. Subsection d(1) gives a first-violation band of 'not more than $500' and a subsequent band of 'not less than $500 nor more than $1,500', which overlap at $500. 'Division on Civil Rights' in subsection f. is not defined in the act.
